text:
That man

is equal to the gods,

seated face to face, listening


to your sweet voice and your enchanting laughter.

That is what stirs a tumult

in my breast. Merely to look at you,

my voice trembles, my tongue fails.

At once a light fire runs

through my limbs; my eyes


go blind and my ears thunder.

Sweat breaks out: a trembling

hounds me. I turn paler

than grass and am nearly dead.

From "W.C.W.: Twelve Versions"

translation.title: Sappho
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragment's bodily sequence and imports only the correctly titled Sappho record.
